worked_solution:
Both the numerator and denominator approach $\infty $ as $x\to \infty .$ However, since ${x}^{5}≫\operatorname{ln}⁡(8x)$ for large values of $x,$ the numerator is growing much faster than the denominator. Consequently, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8x)}=\infty 
$$

Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8x)}+6)=\infty 
$$
